Jasmine / Karthik —

Short answer: yes, we can support a 14-day TTL for request/response traces for a tenant, but it requires a scoped exception and a few compensating controls to be in place. High-level controls I recommend including in the exception document:

1) Tenant-scoped TTL: set request-trace.retention_days = 14 for the Avery tenant. This will expire the logs automatically; we will provide a config snapshot and API sample to demonstrate configuration.

2) Pseudonymization: ensure we mask any headers/body fields that may contain PHI before logging (we have an input-scrubbing pipeline; we can provide the scrub rules and an example pipeline config).

3) Audit-only access: restrict access to the log export/restore APIs to an audit role. All accesses are logged to an immutable audit ledger (S3 with object lock + internal alerting).

4) Read-after-delete verification: on deletion events we record a deletion token and retention-reduction audit entry — we can include a small evidence pack for one sample deletion showing the sequence.

5) Compensating monitoring: set up anomalous access alerts to the tenant logs and weekly rolling export of metadata-only summaries to a customer-owned bucket (optional).

Caveats: we cannot retroactively delete logs that have already been exported to customer-owned archival (if Avery requests archival). Also, debug core dumps and full model KV caches are treated separately; those typically require special handling and are not covered by standard TTLs.

I'll assemble a 1-page exception letter that covers the above and attach the SIG/CAIQ excerpt. Draft ETA: end of day Tue (7/30).
